Lin's concordance statistics per rater and condition

Source: R/sad_conventional.R
sad_ccc.Rd

First stage of the conventional SAD validation: computes Lin's concordance correlation coefficient and its components for each rater under each condition.

Usage

sad_ccc(x)

Arguments

x

An object returned by sad_data().

Value

A tibble with one row per rater and condition and columns n, rho_c, r, Cb, v, u, intercept and slope.

Details

\(\rho_c = r \times C_b\), where \(r\) is Pearson's correlation (precision) and \(C_b = 2 / (v + 1/v + u^2)\) is the bias correction factor (accuracy). \(v = \sigma_{est}/\sigma_{act}\) is the scale shift and \(u = (\mu_{est} - \mu_{act}) / \sqrt{\sigma_{est}\sigma_{act}}\) is the location shift, negative when the rater underestimates. Note that epiR::epi.ccc() reports the location shift with the opposite sign. The intercept and slope of the regression of estimates on actual values are also returned.

References

Lin, L. I. (1989). A concordance correlation coefficient to evaluate reproducibility. Biometrics 45:255-268.

See also

sad_compare()

Examples

x <- sad_data(SADRustSoybean, wide = c(UN = "unaided", SAD = "aided"), group = "sad")
head(sad_ccc(x))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 12
#>   rater group method condition     n rho_c     r    Cb     v       u intercept
#>   <fct> <fct> <fct>  <fct>     <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 1     Old   UN     UN_Old       50 0.901 0.942 0.956  1.05  0.297      7.22 
#> 2 2     Old   UN     UN_Old       50 0.906 0.923 0.982  1.18 -0.0998    -5.85 
#> 3 3     Old   UN     UN_Old       50 0.829 0.915 0.907  1.34  0.346      0.259
#> 4 4     Old   UN     UN_Old       50 0.923 0.927 0.996  1.09  0.0301     0.211
#> 5 5     Old   UN     UN_Old       50 0.771 0.916 0.841  1.36  0.531      4.35 
#> 6 6     Old   UN     UN_Old       50 0.869 0.897 0.969  1.18  0.191      2.31
